header.title: What a session costs before you ask anything
header.lede: About **47.0k tokens** up front, some **0.7k less** than the previous measurement. This time the gain is in the **measured** part: the Chris persona went from 21,300 to **19,165 B** (#2731), and the always-on path now sits at 57% of the budget. The estimated layers were recounted and have not changed.

actions.lede: Ranked by tokens per session. The persona action is checked off and measured; the open actions were checked again against this session and the measurement, and still stand.

items.title: Clear out the remaining connector stubs and the duplicate Asana
items.text: Now the biggest open lever. 21 claude.ai connectors are still there as an `authenticate`/`complete_authentication` pair (42 names). Asana still appears twice: as a stub and as `Asana_2` with 47 tool names.
items.how: In claude.ai → Settings → Connectors, remove what you use nowhere, and drop one of the two Asana connections.
items.caveat: Account-wide: whatever the BWJ repos use costs functionality there.

items.title: `adopt-dkj-policy` behind disable-model-invocation
items.text: Still the most expensive skill description in dkj-policy (850 tokens), measured. It is a one-time adoption step, but it sits in every session of every consumer.
items.how: `disable-model-invocation: true` in the SKILL.md, and have the session check that points to the skill name the command.
items.caveat: The model then no longer triggers it on its own when a session check reports a missing folder.

items.title: Make the chains in Chris's lens on-demand
items.text: The list of chains (~2,000 B) is only needed when a chain is laid out, not on every turn. The lens is unchanged: 13,959 B, now the second-largest document.
items.how: Move it to a place that loads on demand, with a pointer in the lens.
items.caveat: Chris names the chain up front; without the list in context he has to read it first.

items.title: Shorten the connector register in the source repo to a count
items.text: connector-sessioncheck still prints five `[ERROR]` lines about xoxowildhearts here in every session. That is well over half the hook output.
items.how: One line with the count and the command `check-connectors.ps1` for the full overview.
items.caveat: The register is deliberately visible here; a count makes a new error less noticeable.

items.title: Remove `cowork-plugin-management` from the account
items.text: What remains of the synced plugins: two skills (`cowork-plugin-customizer`, `create-cowork-plugin`) that have no work in this repo.
items.how: In claude.ai: Customize → Plugins, switch it off if you do not use it in Cowork.
items.caveat: Account-wide; in Cowork it is the route for building plugins.

items.title: Move more of the Chris persona into the manual
items.text: Done in #2731: the situational rules now live in `specialist-01-01-manual.md`. Measured ~0.7k tokens less; the earlier estimate was ~1.5k, because the two pickup guardrails deliberately stayed always-on.
items.how: The usual chain: branch, PR, fold.
items.caveat: At 19,165 B the persona is still the largest document, but what it holds applies every turn; cutting further costs rules that have to survive a compaction.

items.title: Remove the synced team plugins from claude.ai
items.text: Done: `team-alpha`, `team-ecomm` and `team-shopify` are no longer in the agent list, and the second `orchestrator` skill is gone.
items.caveat: Only `cowork-plugin-management` is left; see the separate action.

items.saveSub: measured on the list: ~4,000 → ~1,700 deferred-name tokens

items.text: The ~130 Klaviyo tool names and the Shopify instructions are no longer in the session; Klaviyo, Shopify and Microsoft 365 now appear only as an authenticate stub.
items.caveat: Connectors are account-wide: the BWJ repos do use Klaviyo and Shopify.

items.title: Switch figma off for this repo
items.text: Done: figma is no longer under `enabledPlugins` in `.claude/settings.json`, and the collect does not find the plugin.
items.caveat: Only life-hub still has figma installed (project scope).

advice.heading: The persona is done: what remains is small
advice.lede: The persona trim yielded a **measured** ~0.7k, less than the estimated 1.5k, because the pickup guardrails deliberately stayed always-on. Not a single open action is above ~1k any more. The always-on path is at 57% of the budget.

steps.title: 1 · Connector stubs and the duplicate Asana (~1k, estimated)
steps.text: The biggest open item, but it is an **estimate**. One pass through claude.ai → Connectors, without changing a single line in the repo. It is account-wide, so check first what the BWJ repos still use. If you get it wrong, it only costs a reconnection.

steps.title: 2 · `adopt-dkj-policy` behind disable-model-invocation (850, measured)
steps.text: The biggest **measured** and direct lever, and the only one that counts in every consumer. It runs through the usual chain. The risk: a session check that reports a missing `dkj-policy/` folder can no longer have the skill trigger on its own. So have that check name the command.

steps.title: 3 · The smaller items
steps.text: Then the chains out of the lens (~600), the connector register as a count (~400) and `cowork-plugin-management` off the account (~150). About 1.1k together.

dont.label: Do not
dont.text: Trim the persona further: at 19,165 B it is still the largest document, but what it holds now applies every turn and has to survive a compaction. The budget is not a problem (42.8k B of headroom), so cutting for the sake of the number makes no sense. The tool definitions (13k) cannot be influenced. And do not repeat the measurement without cause: this run made sense because a document shrank.

footer: Measured: always-on documents (bytes, tokens at 3.12 chars/token, calibrated on August 15, 2026) and plugin skill listings (claude plugin details, count_tokens API, minus disable-model-invocation). Estimated (±30%): tool definitions, harness instructions, deferred tool names, MCP instructions, built-in skills and agents, account skills, synced account plugins, session context and hook output. Method: characters in context divided by ~3.5, or the number of names × ~13. All estimated layers were re-estimated in this session, not carried over. The 15 core agent descriptions are in no measured figure. The repo skill `triage-inbound` (~100 tokens) falls outside both halves. Collect reported no problems; installed and priced version are equal (5.12.0). Step 2 of the skill failed on a short-name `out_dir` (`GEBRUI~1`); without `out_dir` it worked (#2735). Previous measurement: earlier on October 2, 2026.
